hints: Choose a spanning forest and consider edges outside it.
Each non-tree edge can be chosen independently; its choice determines which tree edges are needed for even degrees.
The number of non-tree edges is m-n+c, where c is the number of connected components.
analogy: Every extra edge creates a cycle; combining selected cycles keeps every degree even.
example: A triangle has two Eulerian subgraphs: no edges and all three edges.
algorithm: Count connected components c by DFS or disjoint-set union. Compute 2^(m-n+c) modulo 10^9+7 using fast exponentiation. Isolated vertices count as components.
correctness: Fix arbitrary choices for all non-tree edges. Process each spanning tree from leaves upward: the parent edge is uniquely determined by the parity needed at the child, and the root is automatically even because the sum of degrees is even. Thus every choice gives exactly one Eulerian subgraph.
complexity: For n vertices and m edges, O(n+m+log m) time and O(n+m) space with DFS.
